evidenceFlow.detail: scripts/build_party_trends.py verifies original CSV SHA-256 hashes, counts accepted early-voting records by return date and party registration, then computes running totals. metricDefinitions.label: Daily accepted ballots
metricDefinitions.definition: Each matching original record contributes one ballot to its return date, party-registration group, selected scope and age cohort.

metricDefinitions.label: Cumulative ballots
metricDefinitions.definition: For one year, scope, age cohort and party group, cumulative ballots equal the sum of daily ballots from day 1 through the displayed date. This is a running total, not a turnout rate.

metricDefinitions.label: Party registration
metricDefinitions.definition: DEM = Democratic; REP = Republican; UNA = Unaffiliated. All remaining nonblank registration codes form Other registered parties. Blank codes remain Not specified if observed. Registration does not reveal candidate choice.

metricDefinitions.label: Separate age bands
metricDefinitions.definition: 18–24, 25–34, 35–44, 45–64 and 65–120 do not overlap. Unknown or outside-range ages remain in the all-age total. The legacy 18–22 sensitivity rows are retained in the CSV but are not a separate age-menu band.

metricDefinitions.label: Shared scale ceiling
metricDefinitions.definition: The guide is the highest final cumulative party count among 2022, 2024 and 2026 for the selected scope and age band. The same reviewed maximum sets all three vertical scales; it is not an extra ballot series.

metricDefinitions.label: Final counts, shares and changes
metricDefinitions.definition: Final values use the last matched early-voting day for each year. Share = category count / all selected ballots * 100; count change = 2026 count - baseline count; growth = count change / baseline count * 100; share change = unrounded 2026 share - baseline share, in percentage points. Comparisons retain both 2022 and 2024 baselines. Zero denominators display N/A.

metricDefinitions.label: Residential area
metricDefinitions.definition: Precinct uses precinct_desc; ZIP code uses voter_zip, not a mailing-address field. Original trimmed field text is retained; blank is Unknown / blank. These are recorded residence groups, not the voting site precinct or verified NC State student residence.

metricDefinitions.label: Same-area location use
metricDefinitions.formula: site_share_pct = site_ballots / wake_ballots * 100; wake_ballots = site_ballots + other_wake_ballots
metricDefinitions.definition: For one residential area, year and age band, denominator is its accepted early ballots at ANY Wake location in the matched window. Site is Talley in 2022/2024 and Western Boulevard in 2026. This is site choice among observed early ballots, not resident turnout. Share differences subtract unrounded shares.

metricDefinitions.label: Absent versus zero
metricDefinitions.definition: If an area label has no accepted early ballots of any age in a year, area_present is false and all counts are null. Zero is used only for a cohort within an otherwise observed area. Null shares occur when cohort ballots are zero. Absence does not establish when a precinct was created.

metricDefinitions.label: Comparability
metricDefinitions.definition: Precinct boundaries/labels, populations, ZIP composition and election cycles may change. These independent yearly cohorts do not prove the same individuals switched locations. 2024 is presidential; 2022/2026 are midterms. Mail and Election Day ballots and registered-population denominators are absent.

metricDefinitions.label: Chart selection
metricDefinitions.definition: Rank residential areas by their combined named-site ballots across all three selected years, and show up to ten matching the search. The full table is searchable and paginated. Count and share chart modes use the same areas.

metricDefinitions.label: Full age breakdown for a selected precinct
metricDefinitions.definition: All disjoint age bands are shown together, independent of the map age filter. Count stacks split each age band into named-site and other-Wake ballots. Percentage stacks divide each part by that same age band’s Wake total, not the all-age total. The table retains 2022, 2024 and 2026; its All ages footer equals the sum of the age bands before rounding. Unavailable areas or zero denominators retain N/A.

metricDefinitions.label: Simultaneous precinct age cards and companion area
metricDefinitions.definition: Below the full-width map, all disjoint age bands and a separately labeled All ages combined summary are paired for current precincts 01-23 and 01-31. Each age row aligns both precincts and their 2022, 2024 and 2026 site, other-Wake and total counts. Card headings select the precinct and map age without hiding either comparison area. Card footers subtract 2022 counts and unrounded shares from 2026; share changes are percentage points. Map source inspection includes both complete area age collections and the selected map cohort. The separate selected-area chart and tables remain. No ballot aggregates or age denominators change.

metricDefinitions.label: Precinct ballot growth, 2022 to 2026
metricDefinitions.formula: growth = (2026 count - 2022 count) / 2022 count * 100; absolute change = 2026 count - 2022 count
metricDefinitions.definition: Join the same recorded residential precinct code and selected age cohort in both years. The count is either all accepted early ballots at any Wake location (wake_ballots) or ballots at Talley in 2022 and Western Boulevard in 2026 (site_ballots). Match the first 16 calendar early-voting days. Missing area/year is unavailable, never zero. A zero baseline has undefined percentage growth; a positive current count with zero baseline is separately marked new from zero. Current GIS polygons are a reference, not harmonized historical boundaries; changes may reflect redistricting or population changes as well as voting behavior. No turnout denominator, student identifier or causal estimate is supplied.

metricDefinitions.label: Growth versus Wake County

metricDefinitions.definition: A separate count-weighted county benchmark is calculated for each age group from the full Wake County totals, including unmapped precincts. It is not an average of precinct percentages. Both periods use the same first 16 early-voting days. Negative means slower growth than Wake even when counts rose; positive means faster growth. metricDefinitions.label: Share of modeled trips near site
metricDefinitions.formula: near_share_pct = count(eligible modeled pairs with minimum route-to-selected-distance-basis <= selected radius) / eligible modeled pair count * 100; basis = mapped entrance point (equal circles, default) or whole building footprint (original buffers)
metricDefinitions.definition: Equal-circle mode uses identical ground radii around mapped GIS entrance points, which are not confirmed voting-room doors. Original footprint mode preserves the earlier whole-building buffer calculation. Distances are computed on full-resolution modeled paths, including short entrance connectors. Purple routes and the paginated review list use the exact same basis, radius and eligible-pair filters as the percentage. caveats: No observed student traffic, class schedules, occupancy or destination visitation.
GIS Classroom classification misses teaching inside office/laboratory buildings; dining selection does not include every cafe.
Results depend on destinations, threshold, entrance choice and deterministic shortest routes.
No history reconstruction, visibility model or causal voting inference.
